name: Interactive Task and Concept Learning from Natural Language Instructions and GUI Demonstrations
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its normalized abstract SHA-256 matches the retained bibliographic snapshot. The original API response body was not locally available for this review. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces PUMICE, an agent that learns mobile-app procedures and conditional concepts through natural-language conversation and GUI demonstrations, recursively resolving ambiguous instructions with users.

publication.title: Multimodal Web Navigation with Instruction-Finetuned Foundation Models

name: Multimodal Web Navigation with Instruction-Finetuned Foundation Models
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Trains WebGUM offline from demonstrations by jointly tuning an instruction-following language model and a vision encoder over webpage screenshots and HTML. The agent predicts browser actions and is evaluated on MiniWoB, WebShop, and Mind2Web.

name: Grounded Language Agent for Product Search via Intelligent Web Interactions
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces GLAINTEL, a Flan-T5-based product-search web agent studied under unsupervised learning, demonstration-based training, and unsupervised domain adaptation. It compares ways to combine demonstrations with reinforcement learning.

name: Synatra: Turning Indirect Knowledge into Direct Demonstrations for Digital Agents at Scale
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Synatra converts indirect procedural knowledge, including human-oriented tutorials, into direct demonstrations for digital agents. It trains a 7B CodeLlama on 100,000 synthesized demonstrations and evaluates the resulting policy on Mind2Web, MiniWoB++, and WebArena.

name: AppVLM: A Lightweight Vision Language Model for Online App Control
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: AppVLM first learns app actions from AndroidControl and then refines its policy through data collected in AndroidWorld. The study compares offline action prediction and online task completion for a lightweight vision-language smartphone agent.

name: How to Train Your LLM Web Agent: A Statistical Diagnosis
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Studies compute allocation for web-agent post-training with teacher-generated supervised fine-tuning followed by on-policy reinforcement learning. It samples 1,370 training configurations and uses bootstrap analysis to examine hyperparameter sensitivity on WorkArena and MiniWoB++.

name: SEAgent: Self-Evolving Computer Use Agent with Autonomous Learning from Experience
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: SEAgent explores unfamiliar software using a world-state assessor and an automatically generated task curriculum. It learns from failed and successful interactions through adversarial imitation and GRPO, then combines specialist experience into a generalist agent evaluated on five OSWorld software environments.

name: CODA: Coordinating the Cerebrum and Cerebellum for a Dual-Brain Computer Use Agent with Decoupled Reinforcement Learning
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: CODA combines a generalist planner with a specialist GUI executor and trains application-specific planners through decoupled GRPO. Successful specialist trajectories then support supervised training of a consolidated planner, evaluated across four ScienceBoard applications.

name: UIPro: Unleashing Superior Interaction Capability For GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: UIPro pretrains GUI understanding on 20.6 million tasks and then harmonizes interaction datasets through a unified action space. Continued fine-tuning uses the merged multi-platform data to train action prediction for generalist GUI operation.

name: Retrieval-augmented GUI Agents with Generative Guidelines
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract. Experiments and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: RAG-GUI trains a small guidance adapter to filter and summarize retrieved web tutorials while keeping the acting agent fixed. Supervised and rejection-sampling stages prepare the adapter for inference-time assistance, tested on offline web/mobile tasks and interactive Android tasks.

name: Scaling Synthetic Task Generation for Agents via Exploration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: AutoPlay explores application states and functions to generate tasks, then uses a model executor and verifier to construct demonstrations. It produces 20,000 tasks across 20 Android apps and 10,000 tasks across 13 Ubuntu apps for supervised and reinforcement learning of UI agents.

name: UI-Voyager: A Self-Evolving GUI Agent Learning via Failed Experience
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces a two-stage mobile GUI learner that first co-evolves trajectories and policies through rejection fine-tuning. Group Relative Self-Distillation then uses successful rollout branches to provide step-level supervision for failed trajectories, evaluated on AndroidWorld.

name: MolmoWeb: Open Visual Web Agent and Open Data for the Open Web
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced. The abstract states that artifacts will be released; this annotation does not independently verify release status or licenses.
summary: Presents MolmoWebMix, combining synthetic browser trajectories, human demonstrations and GUI perception data, and MolmoWeb screenshot-to-action policies trained from it. Browser benchmarks also test parallel rollouts with best-of-N selection.

name: OpenMobile: Building Open Mobile Agents with Task and Trajectory Synthesis
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Presents OpenMobile, which builds exploration-based environment memory to synthesize task instructions and switches between learner and expert policies during trajectory collection. The resulting data includes recovery behavior and is tested through mobile-agent training and benchmark-overlap analysis.

name: Mem-W: Latent Memory-Native GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Experimental results and artifact availability have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces Mem-W, which compresses previous trajectories and current-session segments into latent memory tokens used directly by the GUI policy. Self-distillation and outcome supervision train this memory representation for web and mobile navigation.

name: UI-MOPD: Multi-Platform On-Policy Distillation for Unified GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. Experimental results and released artifacts have not been independently reproduced.
summary: Introduces Uni-GUI, a collection of executable desktop and mobile trajectories, and UI-MOPD, which trains a shared policy from its own rollouts using platform-specific teachers. The distillation procedure routes each visited state to the appropriate teacher to preserve distinct interaction conventions.

name: ASIL: Replacing Screenshot-and-Click with Structured State and Semantic Actions
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Experimental findings and release availability have not been independently reproduced or verified.
summary: ASIL exposes application state as structured JSON and provides code-executable semantic actions. Its application benchmark compares this interface with screenshot control and application-native APIs, and studies supervised and reinforcement learning on the structured interface.
